Chapter VA group insolvency and Section 240C cross-border provisions being carved out of the May 2026 commencement notification with no rules framed, and the draft's explicit correction of commentary that wrongly describes India as having adopted the UNCITRAL Model Law, independently confirmed via iPleaders' dedicated analysis, which also separately confirms tribunals are still handling such cases through ad hoc judicial improvisation. Penalty Schedule figures (250 crore security safeguards/s.8(5), 200 crore each for breach notification/s.8(6) and children's data/s.9, 150 crore significant data fiduciary/s.10, 50 crore residual, assessed per instance not as an annual cap) independently confirmed across two sources matching exactly. Appeal route (Board order to TDSAT within 60 days, s.29, further appeal to Supreme Court on questions of law under s.30) confirmed, including TDSAT's own six-month disposal mandate. Consent manager conditions (Rule 4, Part A First Schedule, 2 crore net worth up from a 20-million draft figure, Indian incorporation, independent interoperability certification with technical standards still pending from the Board) confirmed. Children's data provisions (18-year threshold, verifiable parental/guardian consent, Digital Locker/Rule 10 identity verification route, bar on tracking and targeted advertising to minors subject to limited exceptions) confirmed, though most detailed commentary available was still describing the January 2025 draft rather than confirming final Rules text, which the article's own verification_notes already and correctly flag as a limitation rather than asserting false certainty. Cross-border transfer blacklist model (Rule 15, transfer permitted unless a destination is specifically restricted, no restricted-country notification found) confirmed, as was the genuine, unresolved status of the breach-notification '72 hours' figure, which independent sources likewise could trace only to the January 2025 draft rather than confirmed final Rules text; the article's explicit hedging on this exact point ('reported in current compliance commentary... has not been entirely uniform') is accurate and appropriately cautious rather than an error. Both related_pages paths exist in origin/main:assets/search-index.json. No client anecdotes or marketing language present. This draft's verification_notes are unusually disciplined about flagging precisely the points (exact notification day, further-appeal forum, breach-notification hour figure, survival of the critical-personal-data cross-border rule) where the underlying Rules text could not be confirmed, rather than resolving them by invention.
